brief: 6 productivity tips from a designer who built a 7-figure studio.

slots.headline: Six productivity habits that scaled my studio to seven figures.

slots.title: Time-block deep work
slots.body: Protect three-hour windows for design without Slack or email. Your best creative output demands uninterrupted focus. Treat these blocks as non-negotiable client meetings.

slots.title: Build design systems
slots.body: Reusable components cut delivery time in half immediately. Start with type, color, and spacing rules every project shares. Consistency is a profit multiplier.

slots.title: Automate onboarding early
slots.body: Use templates for contracts, briefs, and welcome emails. Automation removes repetitive admin so you can bill for creativity, not inbox management.

slots.title: Kill scope creep fast
slots.body: Define deliverables in writing before any work begins. When requests drift, quote a change order same-day. Boundaries protect margins and sanity.

slots.title: Batch admin tasks
slots.body: Group invoicing, emails, and updates into one afternoon. Switching contexts kills momentum; batching keeps the rest of your week free for making.

slots.title: Protect your mornings
slots.body: Tackle your hardest creative work before noon. Willpower depletes as the day progresses, so guard early hours like they are billable gold.

slots.headline: Build a studio that runs itself.
slots.body: Steal the exact templates and systems I used to grow. Your creative business deserves better margins.
